Hi! I'm picking up TEXTKIT-120 (render_template). The ticket description mentions you have the notes from the design review about edge-case decisions for this function. Could you share those with me? I want to make sure the current implementation aligns with them before running acceptance checks.

Hi! On TEXTKIT-114: in the design review we agreed initials never end a sentence — a single uppercase letter + period (optionally after an opening quote/bracket), e.g. "J. R. R. Tolkien" or "Harry S. Truman", is not a boundary even if the next word is capitalized.

Re render_template edge cases: None renders as empty string (""), never as "None". Other falsy values render normally (0 -> "0", False -> "False"). That's what was agreed in the design review. Let me know if you need anything else!

From the design review: candidates with equal scores keep the order in which they were supplied (editors list preferred tags first); ties must NOT be re-sorted alphabetically or by length. So for rank_matches("cat", ["hat", "bat", "cut", "cat"]) the order is ("cat",1.0), ("hat",0.67), ("bat",0.67), ("cut",0.67) — preserve input order among ties.

Hi! Yes, I have the notes from the design review for split_identifier. The key decision is: Runs of capital letters are acronyms and stay together as one word, except when an uppercase run is followed by a lowercase letter, the last capital of the run starts the next word. Examples: "parseHTTPResponse" -> ["parse", "http", "response"], "XMLParser" -> ["xml", "parser"], "getURL" -> ["get", "url"]. Hope that helps!
